content:
The [Macro Calculator](/macro-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Split daily calories into protein, carbohydrate and fat grams. Enter your daily calories, protein and fat and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Split daily calories into protein, carbohydrate and fat grams. This free online macro calculator gives you an instant answer without an account, a download or sending your entries to a server. It is designed for quick everyday use on desktop and mobile. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the Macro Calculator

Start by entering your daily calories (kcal), then entering your protein (%) and finally entering your fat (%). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Enter your daily calories (kcal).
2. Enter your protein (%).
3. Enter your fat (%).
4. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
5. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

Protein and carbohydrate provide 4 kcal/g; fat provides 9 kcal/g. Carbohydrate is the remaining percentage.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Macro Calculator](/macro-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. At 2,200 kcal with 30% protein, 30% fat and 40% carbs: 165 g protein, 220 g carbs and 73 g fat. Try the same figures in the [Macro Calculator](/macro-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Daily calories: 2200 kcal, Protein: 30 %, Fat: 30 %), the [Macro Calculator](/macro-calculator) returns Protein: 165 g, Carbohydrate: 220 g, Fat: 73.3 g, Carbohydrate share: 40%. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [BMI Calculator](/bmi-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Check the units and labels before comparing results.
- Your entries stay in your browser and are not saved.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is this macro calculator free?

Yes. It is free to use, with no sign-up or installation required. There is no limit on how often you use it, nothing to install, and no account to create — open the [Macro Calculator](/macro-calculator) and start straight away.

### Are my entries stored?

No. Calculations run in your browser and the tool does not save your entries. You can use it as often as you like, and because nothing is uploaded, stored or tracked, there is nothing to delete afterwards.

### What formula does the Macro Calculator use?

Protein and carbohydrate provide 4 kcal/g; fat provides 9 kcal/g. Carbohydrate is the remaining percentage. You can see it in action in the [Macro Calculator](/macro-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the Macro Calculator?

Just Daily calories, Protein and Fat. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.

### How accurate is the Macro Calculator?

It applies the standard formula to the values you enter, so the result is as accurate as your inputs. Treat it as an estimate for informational use. For figures that matter, such as money, health or legal deadlines, check the result against an authoritative source before acting on it.
